subtasks.title: Add revert config interface, defaults, and validation
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: config.ts uses safeGet(obj,key) for Proxy-safe field access, coerceBoolean(v,fallback) for booleans, coerceNumber(field,v,fallback,mustBePositive) for numbers, warnConfig(field,value) for logging, isRecord(value) for object checks. The outer validateConfig has a try/catch that NEVER throws — per-field failures fall back to defaults with a warn. DEFAULT_CONFIG is structuredClone'd as the base. The new revert block follows the exact same pattern as the existing rewind/shrink/nudges blocks. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/codebase_patterns.md §1.
2. INPUT: The existing MulliganConfig interface and DEFAULT_CONFIG in src/config.ts. The existing validateConfig function with its safeGet/coerce pattern.
3. LOGIC: Add `revert` to MulliganConfig interface with fields: enabled:boolean, allowDeleteCreatedFiles:boolean, nonGitMode:"cas"|"explicit-paths", storageDir:string|null, maxFileBytes:number, maxTotalBytes:number, maxSnapshotsPerTurn:number, excludeGlobs:string[]. Add to DEFAULT_CONFIG: {enabled:false, allowDeleteCreatedFiles:false, nonGitMode:"cas", storageDir:null, maxFileBytes:262144, maxTotalBytes:33554432, maxSnapshotsPerTurn:64, excludeGlobs:[".git","node_modules","dist","build",".next",".venv","target"]}. Add to validateConfig: `const revertRaw = safeGet(raw, "revert"); if (isRecord(revertRaw)) { ... }` with per-field coercion: enabled/allowDeleteCreatedFiles via coerceBoolean; nonGitMode validated ∈ {"cas","explicit-paths"} (else default+warn); storageDir validated as string that MUST NOT resolve inside cwd via path.resolve comparison (else null+warn); maxFileBytes/maxTotalBytes/maxSnapshotsPerTurn via coerceNumber(_,_,_,true); excludeGlobs validated as string array (non-array → default list). Verify settings.ts deep-merge recurses into the new revert block (it should — verify no change needed). Write config validation tests: boolean coercion, nonGitMode domain, storageDir inside cwd rejection, number finite>0, excludeGlobs array coercion.
4. OUTPUT: MulliganConfig.revert is the typed config block, accessible via getConfig().revert. All downstream phases consume this.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc on the revert interface block + each field in src/config.ts, citing @14 §8 and spec/09 §2/§3. These ride WITH the work.

tasks.title: Create src/snapshot/paths.ts (pure path safety helpers)
tasks.description: New file with zero Pi imports. Implements resolveSafeWorkspacePath, normalizeRelPath, isDangerousWorkspaceRel per spec/14 §4.3. Rejects .. escape, NUL bytes, directory paths, .git/.pi/node_modules, absolute paths outside workspace root.

subtasks.title: Implement pure path safety helpers
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: This is a brand-new file with ZERO imports from Pi or other project modules. It is fully unit-testable in isolation. The functions enforce path safety for the snapshot backends (both git and CAS) — they prevent the backends from writing outside the workspace or touching sensitive directories. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/external_deps.md §2.
2. INPUT: No external inputs — pure functions taking (workspaceRoot: string, candidatePath: string) and returning safe/resolved paths or throwing/rejecting.
3. LOGIC: Implement per spec/14 §4.3:
   - resolveSafeWorkspacePath(workspaceRoot, relPath): resolves relPath against workspaceRoot using path.resolve, then verifies the result is INSIDE workspaceRoot (no .. escape). Returns the absolute path. Throws on escape attempt.
   - normalizeRelPath(workspaceRoot, absPath): converts an absolute path to a workspace-relative POSIX path (forward slashes). Returns the rel path string.
   - isDangerousWorkspaceRel(relPath): returns true for paths that must NEVER be captured/restored: paths containing NUL bytes, paths escaping via .., directory paths (ending in /), paths under .git/.pi/node_modules, absolute paths that resolve outside workspace root.
   All functions are PURE — no fs calls, no side effects. Export all three.
4. OUTPUT: Three exported pure functions consumed by src/snapshot/git.ts (P2.M2.T1) and src/snapshot/cas.ts (P2.M3.T1) for path validation during capture and restore.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on each exported function citing @14 §4.3. Rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: Create src/snapshot/store.ts (interface + factory + mutex)
tasks.description: The central store module: interface definition, type exports, AsyncMutex serialization primitive, and the detectAndCreate factory that picks the right backend.

subtasks.title: SnapshotStore interface + types + AsyncMutex
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The SnapshotStore interface is the contract both backends implement. AsyncMutex serializes ALL operations on a given store instance (capture/dirtyCheck/restore/retire must never overlap). The interface is defined here and implemented by git.ts and cas.ts in P2.M2/P2.M3. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/system_context.md.
2. INPUT: RevertCheckpoint type from P1.M2.T2.S1 (markers.ts). The MulliganConfig.revert block from P1.M1.T1.S1 (config.ts).
3. LOGIC: Define and EXPORT: interface SnapshotStore { describe(): { backend: "git"|"cas"|"none"; reason?: string }; capture(label: string): string | null; dirtyCheck(afterRef: string, paths: string[]): string[]; restore(beforeRef: string, opts: RestoreOpts): RestoreResult; has(ref: string): boolean; retire(ref: string): void; }. Define and EXPORT: interface RestoreOpts { revertFileChanges: boolean; deleteCreatedFiles: boolean; }. Define and EXPORT: interface RestoreResult { reverted: string[]; deleted: string[]; failed: string[]; skipped: string[]; refused: string[]; }. Implement and EXPORT class AsyncMutex { acquire(): Promise<() => void> } — serializes async operations via a promise chain. Write unit tests for AsyncMutex (verify serialization: concurrent calls execute sequentially).
4. OUTPUT: The SnapshotStore interface + types exported from store.ts, consumed by git.ts (P2.M2.T1), cas.ts (P2.M3.T1), rewind.ts (P4.M2.T1), and index.ts (P3.M1.T2). AsyncMutex is also exported for use by the backend constructors.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on SnapshotStore interface, each method, RestoreOpts, RestoreResult, and AsyncMutex citing @14 §2. Rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: detectAndCreate factory (backend detection)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: detectAndCreate decides which backend to use: if the cwd is a git repo (git rev-parse --git-dir succeeds), use GitBackend; if not a git repo but the storage dir is writable, use CasBackend (with config.revert.nonGitMode selecting cas vs explicit-paths); if neither, return a no-op "none" store. This function is called once per session and the result is cached on SessionRuntime. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/external_deps.md §1.
2. INPUT: cwd: string (the working-tree root from ctx.cwd), config: the revert config block from getConfig().revert. The SnapshotStore interface from P2.M1.T1.S1. GitBackend from P2.M2.T1 (imported dynamically), CasBackend from P2.M3.T1 (imported dynamically).
3. LOGIC: EXPORT async function detectAndCreate(cwd: string, revertConfig): Promise<SnapshotStore>. Steps: (1) try `git rev-parse --git-dir` via execFile in cwd — if exit code 0, create and return new GitBackend(cwd, revertConfig); (2) if not git, check if storageDir is writable (mkdir -p then access check) — if writable, create and return new CasBackend(cwd, revertConfig); (3) if neither, return a NoOpStore where describe() returns {backend:"none", reason:"no git and storage unwritable"} and all other methods are no-ops. Wrap in try/catch — on ANY error, return the NoOpStore (E28 fail-open). NOTE: This subtask will be completed AFTER P2.M2.T1 and P2.M3.T1 since it imports them. The NoOpStore can be defined inline in store.ts now; the GitBackend/CasBackend imports will resolve once those phases complete.
4. OUTPUT: A detectAndCreate(cwd, config) function that returns a SnapshotStore instance. Called from index.ts session_start handler (P3.M1.T2).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on detectAndCreate citing @14 §2. Rides WITH the work.

milestones.title: GitBackend — external shadow repository
milestones.description: Create src/snapshot/git.ts implementing the SnapshotStore interface via an external git shadow repository. All writes target GIT_DIR=<storageDir>/<key>; the user's .git is never touched (except read-only rev-parse).

tasks.title: Implement GitBackend (src/snapshot/git.ts)
tasks.description: The external shadow-repo backend. init sets up GIT_DIR=<storageDir>/<key> + GIT_WORK_TREE=<repoRoot>. capture uses add --all -f + write-tree + commit-tree + update-ref. dirtyCheck diffs against afterRef. restore uses read-tree + checkout -- <paths>. The five git-safety guarantees are enforced.

subtasks.title: GitBackend init + capture
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: GitBackend uses child_process.execFile("git", args, {env: {...process.env, GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE}}). The shadow repo is separate from the user's .git. capture forces gitignored files IN (--all -f) and uses pathspec negations from excludeGlobs. The key for <storageDir>/<key> is derived from the repo root path (safe-hash to avoid path collisions). See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/external_deps.md §1.
2. INPUT: SnapshotStore interface from P2.M1.T1.S1. Pure path helpers from P1.M2.T1.S1 (paths.ts — for validating paths during capture). The revert config block from P1.M1.T1.S1 (storageDir, excludeGlobs, maxFileBytes, maxTotalBytes, maxSnapshotsPerTurn). AsyncMutex from P2.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: EXPORT class GitBackend implements SnapshotStore:
   - constructor(cwd: string, revertConfig): store cwd, config, resolve storageDir (config.storageDir ?? path.join(sessionDir, "mulligan")), compute key from cwd.
   - async init(): run `git init --bare` with GIT_DIR=<storageDir>/<key>. Idempotent (skip if exists).
   - describe(): {backend:"git"}.
   - async capture(label: string): acquire mutex; run `git add --all -f` with pathspec negations `:!glob1 :!glob2` from excludeGlobs; run `git write-tree` → treeSha; run `git commit-tree <treeSha> [-p <parent>] -m "snapshot:<label>"` → commitSha; run `git update-ref refs/mulligan/snapshots/<label> <commitSha>`; return commitSha. On ANY error → return null (best-effort). Enforce maxFileBytes/maxTotalBytes/maxSnapshotsPerTurn caps (skip files > maxFileBytes with warn; stop capture if maxTotalBytes exceeded).
   - ALL git commands use GIT_DIR=<shadow> + GIT_WORK_TREE=<cwd> env vars. NEVER use the source repo's .git for writes.
   Write unit tests: mock execFile, assert command construction (add --all -f, write-tree, commit-tree, update-ref), assert NO write command targets sourceGitDir.
4. OUTPUT: GitBackend class implementing capture(). Consumed by detectAndCreate (P2.M1.T1.S2) and rewind.ts step 6b (P4.M2.T1).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on GitBackend class + capture method citing @14 §3 (the five git-safety guarantees). Rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: GitBackend dirtyCheck + restore + retire + has
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: dirtyCheck compares the current working tree against the afterRef snapshot to detect post-turn drift. restore writes working-tree files ONLY (never source index/refs). retire deletes a snapshot ref. The five git-safety guarantees apply to ALL operations. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/external_deps.md §1.
2. INPUT: GitBackend class from P2.M2.T1.S1 (extends this class). SnapshotStore interface from P2.M1.T1.S1. Pure path helpers from P1.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Add methods to GitBackend:
   - async dirtyCheck(afterRef: string, paths: string[]): acquire mutex; run `git diff --name-only <afterRef> -- <paths>` (using shadow repo); return the list of drifted paths. If afterRef is null/missing, return [] (no drift baseline → allow).
   - async restore(beforeRef: string, opts: RestoreOpts): acquire mutex; if opts.revertFileChanges: run `git read-tree <beforeRef>` then `git checkout -- <paths>` (working-tree only, using shadow GIT_DIR + GIT_WORK_TREE); collect reverted/failed paths (catch per-file write errors → failed[]). If opts.deleteCreatedFiles AND config.allowDeleteCreatedFiles: delete files that existed in afterRef but not beforeRef (use fs.unlink, collect deleted/failed). Return RestoreResult {reverted, deleted, failed, skipped, refused}.
   - has(ref: string): run `git rev-parse --verify <ref>` (shadow repo) → boolean.
   - retire(ref: string): run `git update-ref -d <ref>` (shadow repo). 
   - NEVER touch sourceGitDir except read-only rev-parse.
   Write unit tests: mock execFile, assert restore uses read-tree + checkout (not source index), assert retire deletes the ref.
4. OUTPUT: Complete GitBackend implementing the full SnapshotStore interface. Consumed by detectAndCreate (P2.M1.T1.S2), capture hooks (P3.M1.T1), and rewind.ts step 6b (P4.M2.T1).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on dirtyCheck/restore/retire citing @14 §3/§6. Rides WITH the work.

milestones.title: CasBackend — content-addressed store + non-git modes
milestones.description: Create src/snapshot/cas.ts implementing the SnapshotStore interface via a minimal content-addressed store. Supports 'cas' mode (whole-tree walk with mtime short-circuit) and 'explicit-paths' mode (capture only write/edit tool paths).

tasks.title: Implement CasBackend (src/snapshot/cas.ts)
tasks.description: The universal non-git backend. ~300 LOC: SHA-256 hashing, blob dedupe, JSON manifest, mtime/size short-circuit for cas mode, explicit-paths capture for the conservative mode, dirtyCheck via hash equality, restore via blob write, retire via manifest delete.

subtasks.title: CAS hash + blob store + manifest format
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The CAS backend stores content blobs in <storageDir>/blobs/<sha256-prefix>/<sha256> and manifests in <storageDir>/manifests/<label>.json. Blobs are content-deduped (same content → same hash → stored once). The manifest maps {path → {hash, size, mtime, existed}}. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/external_deps.md §2.
2. INPUT: SnapshotStore interface from P2.M1.T1.S1. Pure path helpers from P1.M2.T1.S1. The revert config block from P1.M1.T1.S1 (storageDir, maxFileBytes, maxTotalBytes, excludeGlobs). AsyncMutex from P2.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement and EXPORT class CasBackend implements SnapshotStore:
   - constructor(cwd, revertConfig): store cwd, config, resolve storageDir.
   - Internal: async hashContent(content: Buffer): string (crypto.createHash sha256 hex). async storeBlob(content: Buffer): string (write to <storageDir>/blobs/<prefix>/<hash>, return hash). async readBlob(hash: string): Buffer. 
   - Manifest type: { version:1, label:string, turnIndex:number, ts:number, files: Record<string, {hash:string, size:number, mtime:number, existed:boolean}> }.
   - describe(): {backend:"cas"}.
   Write unit tests: hashContent determinism, storeBlob dedupe (same content → same path, no duplicate write), manifest serialization round-trip.
4. OUTPUT: CasBackend class skeleton with blob/manifest internals. Extended by S2 (capture) and S3 (dirtyCheck/restore).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on CasBackend class + internal helpers citing @14 §4. Rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: CAS 'cas' mode whole-tree capture with mtime short-circuit
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: 'cas' mode (the default nonGitMode) walks the entire workspace tree. The mtime/size short-circuit compares stat.mtimeMs + stat.size against the previous manifest entry — if unchanged, reuse the stored hash (O(changed-files) steady-state). Files matching excludeGlobs are skipped. Files > maxFileBytes are skipped+warned. Total bytes capped by maxTotalBytes. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/external_deps.md §2.
2. INPUT: CasBackend class skeleton from P2.M3.T1.S1 (hash/storeBlob/readBlob/manifest format). Pure path helpers from P1.M2.T1.S1 (isDangerousWorkspaceRel for skip checks).
3. LOGIC: Implement async capture(label: string): acquire mutex; walk cwd tree recursively (fs.readdir + fs.stat); for each file: skip if isDangerousWorkspaceRel or matches excludeGlobs; skip if size > maxFileBytes (warn); check mtime/size against previous manifest (if exists for this label) — if unchanged, reuse hash (short-circuit); else read content, hashContent, storeBlob (if totalBytes budget allows); build manifest entry {hash, size, mtime, existed:true}. Write manifest JSON to <storageDir>/manifests/<label>.json. Return the manifest label as the 'ref'. Track total bytes and snapshot count against caps (E29 — stop accepting new data, mark partial). On ANY error → return null (best-effort).
4. OUTPUT: CasBackend.capture() implementing the comprehensive whole-tree mode. Extended by S3 for dirtyCheck/restore.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on capture method citing @14 §4.1. Rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: CAS explicit-paths mode + dirtyCheck + restore + retire + has
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: 'explicit-paths' mode captures ONLY write/edit tool paths (bash is NOT captured + once-per-turn warning). This is the conservative pi-undo-redo model. dirtyCheck compares current file hashes against the manifest. restore writes pre-span content from blobs. retire deletes the manifest. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/external_deps.md §2.
2. INPUT: CasBackend class from P2.M3.T1.S2 (capture for cas mode, blob/manifest internals). SnapshotStore interface from P2.M1.T1.S1. Pure path helpers from P1.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC:
   - Explicit-paths capture: when config.revert.nonGitMode === "explicit-paths", capture(label, explicitPaths?: string[]) accepts an optional list of paths to capture (from write/edit tool calls). Only those paths are hashed/stored. bash tool paths are NOT captured. Log a once-per-turn warning when bash is detected but not captured.
   - async dirtyCheck(afterRef: string, paths: string[]): read the afterRef manifest; for each path in `paths`, re-hash the current file content; return paths where the hash differs (or file no longer exists). If afterRef is null, return [].
   - async restore(beforeRef: string, opts: RestoreOpts): acquire mutex; read beforeRef manifest; for each file in manifest: if opts.revertFileChanges, readBlob(hash) + writeFile(path, content) → collect reverted/failed; track which files in the after-manifest but NOT in the before-manifest (= created during span) → if opts.deleteCreatedFiles AND config.allowDeleteCreatedFiles, unlink them → collect deleted/failed. Return RestoreResult.
   - has(ref: string): fs.access the manifest file → boolean.
   - retire(ref: string): unlink the manifest file. Optionally mark-sweep unreferenced blobs.
   Write unit tests: explicit-paths capture only captures specified paths; dirtyCheck detects changed file; restore writes pre-span content; deleteCreatedFiles gating.
4. OUTPUT: Complete CasBackend implementing the full SnapshotStore interface for both cas and explicit-paths modes. Consumed by detectAndCreate (P2.M1.T1.S2), capture hooks (P3.M1.T1), and rewind.ts step 6b (P4.M2.T1).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on explicit-paths mode, dirtyCheck, restore, retire citing @14 §4.2/§4.3/§6. Rides WITH the work.

milestones.title: Event hooks + store wiring in index.ts
milestones.description: Register turn_start and agent_end handlers, thread the store through SessionRuntime, and add session_shutdown teardown. The store is created in session_start and destroyed in session_shutdown.

tasks.title: turn_start + agent_end capture hooks
tasks.description: Register two new event handlers (only active when config.revert.enabled). turn_start runs prompt-boundary GC then captures the before-snapshot. agent_end captures the after-snapshot for dirty-check drift detection.

subtasks.title: turn_start hook (prompt-boundary GC + capture 'turn')
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The turn_start event fires at the start of each agent turn. The prompt-boundary GC runs FIRST — it deletes all turn/* snapshot refs (both git refs and CAS manifests) and runs git gc / blob mark-sweep. This is safe because no non-checkpoint rewind crosses a prompt boundary. Then capture("turn") produces the before-ref stored in SessionRuntime.snapshots. The handler must guard on config.revert.enabled AND the store being non-null. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/codebase_patterns.md §6.
2. INPUT: SessionRuntime.snapshots Map from P1.M2.T2.S2 (to store the before-ref). The SnapshotStore from P2.M1.T1.S2 (created by detectAndCreate, accessed via runtime.store). TurnStartEvent { type, turnIndex, timestamp }.
3. LOGIC: Create a registerTurnStartCapture(pi) function (mirrors the existing registerBloatReminder/registerTurnEndMetric pattern). Register pi.on("turn_start", async (event, ctx) => { if (!getConfig().revert.enabled) return; const rt = getRuntime(ctx.sessionId); if (!rt.store) return; try { // GC FIRST: for each key in rt.snapshots starting with "turn", call rt.store.retire(key); also run git gc --auto --prune=now for git backend (or blob mark-sweep for CAS). // THEN CAPTURE: const beforeRef = await rt.store.capture("turn"); if (beforeRef) rt.snapshots.set("turn", {label:"turn", backend: rt.store.describe().backend, beforeRef, turnIndex: event.turnIndex, ts: Date.now()}); } catch { /* best-effort, never throws (E27) */ } }). The handler is async — Pi awaits event handlers.
4. OUTPUT: A registered turn_start handler that maintains SessionRuntime.snapshots.get("turn") as the before-ref for the current turn. Consumed by rewind.ts step 6b (P4.M2.T1.S1) for last_turn revert.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the handler citing @14 §5. Rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: agent_end hook (capture 'turn-after' for dirtyCheck)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The agent_end event fires after the agent finishes its turn (all tool calls + final assistant message). The after-snapshot captures the working-tree state at turn-end. subtasks.title: Step 6b decision tree + checkpoint resolution + dirty guard
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: rewindExecute is a single function in src/tools/rewind.ts with steps 1-9, wrapped in one try/catch (E13). Step 6b goes AFTER marker persist (step ~7 in current numbering), BEFORE mutation warning (step ~8). The revert params come from the tool input (params.revert_file_changes, params.delete_created_files). The checkpoint is resolved from SessionRuntime.snapshots. The dirty guard calls store.dirtyCheck(afterRef, affectedPaths). See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/codebase_patterns.md §4.
2. INPUT: RewindParams with revert_file_changes/delete_created_files from P4.M1.T1.S1. The SnapshotStore interface from P2.M1.T1.S1 (accessed via getRuntime(sessionId).store). SessionRuntime.snapshots Map (P1.M2.T2.S2) holding the turn/ckpt RevertCheckpoints. RewindMarker.revert field from P1.M2.T2.S1 (to populate the marker). The capture hooks from P3.M1.T1 (produce the turn/ckpt checkpoints).
3. LOGIC: After the marker is persisted (appendRewindMarker) and BEFORE the mutation warning, add step 6b:
   - Read params.revert_file_changes and params.delete_created_files (default false for both).
   - If NEITHER is true → skip step 6b entirely (unchanged v1.1 path).
   - If flags set BUT !getConfig().revert.enabled → append "(file revert requested but disabled in config)" to successText, skip restore.
   - If granularity === "last_tool_call_group" → append "File revert applies to last_turn/checkpoint granularity — to also restore files, rewind the whole turn." to successText, skip restore.
   - Else (last_turn or checkpoint): resolve the RevertCheckpoint: for last_turn → rt.snapshots.get("turn"); for checkpoint → rt.snapshots.get("ckpt:" + params.checkpoint). If missing → 0 reverted, append notice, skip restore (best-effort). If found: run dirty guard: const driftedPaths = store.dirtyCheck(checkpoint.afterRef ?? checkpoint.beforeRef, affectedPaths); if driftedPaths.length > 0 → ALL file-revert refused: append "(file revert refused: <N> path(s) changed since the turn ended — not overwritten; re-request if intended)" to successText, set revertRefused=true, skip restore.
   - Pass the revertResult (or refusal) to the next subtask (P4.M2.T1.S2) for the actual restore + marker fold.
4. OUTPUT: The step 6b decision tree runs, resolving the checkpoint and running the dirty guard. The result (proceed/refuse/skip) is consumed by P4.M2.T1.S2 for the actual restore.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on step 6b citing @spec/05 §1 step 6b + @14 §6/§7. Rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: store.restore + fold results into marker.revert + success text
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: When the decision tree in P4.M2.T1.S1 allows the restore, this subtask calls store.restore(beforeRef, {revertFileChanges, deleteCreatedFiles}) and folds the RestoreResult into the success text + the marker's revert field. The success text extension follows spec/05 §1 step 6b verbatim. The marker.revert field structure is defined in markers.ts (P1.M2.T2.S1). See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/codebase_patterns.md §4.
2. INPUT: The decision tree result from P4.M2.T1.S1 (proceed to restore + the resolved RevertCheckpoint). The SnapshotStore from SessionRuntime. RestoreOpts/RestoreResult types from store.ts (P2.M1.T1.S1). The RewindMarker.revert field structure from P1.M2.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: When the decision tree allows restore: `const restoreResult = await store.restore(checkpoint.beforeRef, {revertFileChanges: params.revert_file_changes === true, deleteCreatedFiles: params.delete_created_files === true});` Then fold into success text: append `" Reverted ${restoreResult.reverted.length} file(s), deleted ${restoreResult.deleted.length}; ${restoreResult.skipped.length + restoreResult.failed.length} skipped/failed, ${restoreResult.refused.length} refused (see log)."`. Then build the marker revert block: `revert: { revertedFiles: restoreResult.reverted, deletedFiles: restoreResult.deleted, failedFiles: restoreResult.failed, refusedFiles: restoreResult.refused, skipped: restoreResult.skipped.length > 0, backend: store.describe().backend }`. This block must be included in the payload passed to appendRewindMarker (rides the spread like checkpoint). NOTE: the marker is ALREADY persisted in the earlier step — so either (a) delay the marker persist until after step 6b so the revert field is included, OR (b) append a follow-up marker amendment. Option (a) is cleaner: move appendRewindMarker AFTER step 6b so the revert field is part of the original marker entry. Verify this doesn't break the existing step ordering.
4. OUTPUT: The success text includes revert results. The persisted marker carries the revert audit block. The RewindDetails payload may include revert summary.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The success text format is the LLM-facing contract (spec/05 §1). Rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Conditional E5 mutation warning text for reverted spans
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: MUTATION_WARNING is a module-local const string in rewind.ts. It's appended to successText when the ledger's modifiedFiles/bashSideEffects is non-empty AND config.rewind.requireMutationWarning is true. When step 6b reverted files, the warning must be reworded: the FILE-STATE portion of the effects is restored, so the warning names only effects that are NOT working-tree file state. See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/architecture/codebase_patterns.md §4.
2. INPUT: The MUTATION_WARNING const + the success text builder in rewind.ts. The revert result from P4.M2.T1.S2 (to know whether files were reverted).
3. LOGIC: Add a second const MUTATION_WARNING_REVERTED for the reworded version: `"⚠ The hidden span ran side-effecting commands (see note). Non-filesystem effects PERSIST on disk (commits made, dependency installs, network/DB/process effects, staged index changes). Any files in 'failed' or 'refused' were NOT restored — do not blindly redo those. All other file modifications were reverted to their pre-span state."`. In the success text builder: if step 6b reverted files (revertResult.reverted.length > 0), use MUTATION_WARNING_REVERTED instead of MUTATION_WARNING. The logic is: `const warning = (reverted && revertResult.reverted.length > 0) ? MUTATION_WARNING_REVERTED : MUTATION_WARNING;`.
4. OUTPUT: The agent sees the correct warning depending on whether files were reverted. No false "files persist" message when they were actually restored.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The warning text is the LLM-facing contract. Rides WITH the work.
